findings.title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in UI
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` that prop is `props.onChanged`, which most callers (e.g. /apps/installed/calendar) do not pass. Unlike `disconnectMutation`, there is no `onSettled` that calls `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`. As a result, after a successful cache deletion the dropdown continues to show "Cache Status / Last updated: ..." and the "Delete cached data" action for data that no longer exists until the user hard-refreshes. Add an invalidation of `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` on settle.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId on selected calendars, breaking other callers
findings.body: `UserWithCalendars` is tightened so that `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` must include `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. Only the session-user select in `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated to provide these. `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` is also exported for `@calcom/platform-libraries` (legacy `getConnectedDestinationCalendars`) and consumed by API v2 and other callers that build the user object from `withSelectedCalendars` over a narrower select; those callers will now fail type-checking (or need an extra DB column in every query) even though neither new field is actually read anywhere in this PR. The frontend uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache, so this type change appears unnecessary and should be reverted or the fields made optional.

findings.title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, reporting expired rows as live cache
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows by credential with no `expiresAt: { gte: now }` filter. `getCachedAvailability` only serves rows that have not expired, so a credential whose only rows are expired (e.g. subscription lapsed a month ago) will still show a "Cache Status / Last updated" entry and a delete action in the UI even though no cache is being served. The status should apply the same `expiresAt` filter as the read path, or expose expiry separately.

findings.title: Unused extra write to every SelectedCalendar on each webhook/cache refresh
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now runs `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` after every cache refresh (triggered by every Google webhook and by unwatch). This issues an `UPDATE ... SET updatedAt = now()` across all SelectedCalendar rows for the credential solely to bump `@updatedAt`, but the PR's own description notes this value is not used anywhere in the UI (the frontend reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt`). It adds write load and row-lock contention on a hot path for no consumer. Either remove it or add the consumer that needs it.

findings.title: Access-denied case throws a plain Error, surfacing as 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
findings.body: When the credential does not exist or belongs to another user the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps non-`TRPCError` exceptions to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, so clients get a 500 (and it will be reported as a server error in monitoring) for what is a 404/403 client condition. Other handlers in this router use `TRPCError` with `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN`; this one should too.

findings.title: Instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly, bypassing the calendar-cache feature flag
findings.body: The handler calls `new CalendarCacheRepository()` instead of `CalendarCache.init(...)`/`CalendarCache.initFromCredentialId`, which returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the `calendar-cache` feature is disabled. This means an extra `groupBy` query on `CalendarCache` is executed on every connectedCalendars load for all users, including those for whom the feature is off and the table has no relevant rows. The mock's new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` method is therefore never reached from this code path.

findings.title: Timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded en-US locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's locale and time format preferences, so non-English users see US-formatted dates (MM/DD/YY, 12-hour) inside an otherwise translated menu. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (or the existing dayjs helpers with the user's timeFormat) for consistency with the rest of the app.

findings.title: Migration header warning contradicts the actual SQL
findings.body: The header states the column was "Added ... without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the statement below adds the column `NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`. The stale auto-generated warning is misleading to anyone auditing migrations for data-safety; it should be removed or reworded to match the SQL.

findings.title: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only; fails on Linux
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is the macOS/BSD form of in-place editing. GNU sed (Linux, most CI/dev containers) interprets `''` as a filename and errors with "can't read : No such file or directory", so `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never updated. Additionally `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory rather than the script location, so running `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root writes to a `.env` outside the repository. Use a portable approach (e.g. `sed -i.bak` then remove, or a temp file) and resolve the env path from `$(dirname "$0")`.

findings.title: dev:cron uses npx tsx but tsx is not a declared dependency
findings.body: `dev:cron` now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, yet `tsx` is not listed in `dependencies` or `devDependencies` (only `ts-node` is). `npx` will attempt a network download at run time with an unpinned version, which fails offline and is non-reproducible. Add `tsx` to devDependencies (and invoke it via `tsx` rather than `npx tsx`), or keep `ts-node`.

findings.title: No tests for new deleteCache handler or cache-status repository method
findings.body: The PR adds a destructive mutation (`deleteCacheHandler`), a new repository query (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), and enrichment logic in `connectedCalendarsHandler`, but includes no unit or integration tests. In particular the ownership check (another user's credentialId must be rejected) and the credential→updatedAt mapping are untested; the PR description itself says local testing was not possible. Add tests for the rejection path and for the mapping with multiple cache rows per credential.
